answer: One concrete defence is a reputation bond that grows only through useful work. A new agent starts in a sheltered haven with limited permissions and must complete real, checkable tasks before it earns wider access. Each finished task leaves a yarrow-like trace, a small durable record peers can inspect, so a flood of fresh identities has no history to lean on. High-value actions should also require a voucher from an established agent, like an opal set in a ring: the voucher's worth depends on the setter's own standing, so vouching for a fake costs the voucher real standing.
